title: Clear everyday sentences: word order and time phrases

sections.title: Lesson notes
sections.content: We practised building clear everyday sentences with a subject, verb, object and time phrase.

questions.prompt: What usually comes first in an English statement?
Choose the natural order.
Choose the correct preposition: ___ Monday.
Choose the correct preposition: ___ the evening.

sections.title: Grammar practice
sections.content: Use subject + verb + object, then add place and time when needed.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: My brother ___ the bus to work.
Choose the question with correct word order.
Choose the correct sentence.
Fill in the blank: We meet ___ Friday afternoon.

sections.title: Vocabulary
sections.content: Use daily routine and time words in complete sentences.

questions.prompt: A routine is something you do regularly.
Choose the word that means “not the same each time”.
Fill in the blank: I ___ breakfast before work.
Which phrase means “at the end of the day”?

sections.title: Reading
sections.content: Read everyday routines and notice the order of information in each sentence.

questions.prompt: A clear routine sentence normally starts with …
Time phrases often come …
choices: at the end of the sentence

sections.title: Listening
sections.content: Listen for routine actions, places and times.

questions.prompt: Listen once for the speaker’s routine.
On the second listen, write down …
choices: one action and one time phrase

sections.title: Final review
sections.content: Check grammar and useful everyday vocabulary.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence with natural everyday word order.
Fill in the blank: ___ do you usually leave home?
Choose the correct phrase.
Which word means “happening often”?
